name: Epson to Paperless
summary: Pulls a scan from an Epson scanner on your network and files it straight into Paperless-ngx.

catalog.description: Epson to Paperless asks an Epson scanner on your network for a scan, then uploads the result to Paperless-ngx over its API. Under MOS a scan is started by an HTTP request to this app rather than by the Scan button on the scanner's own panel: the panel path needs the app to sit directly on your home network, which MOS does not give an app it has not reviewed. Everything after the trigger is the same — the app talks to the scanner, collects the pages, and files the document.

features.title: Scan straight into Paperless
features.body: Pages go from the scanner to Paperless-ngx without a shared folder, a watched directory, or a second machine in between.

features.title: Triggered by a request you control
features.body: A token MOS generates at install guards the trigger, so a phone shortcut, a home-automation rule, or a smart button can start a scan.

features.title: A failed upload keeps the pages
features.body: Scans are written to the app's own storage first and only removed once Paperless has accepted them.

resourceHint.label: Low
resourceHint.description: A single small Node process that does nothing between scans.

privacy.summary: Talks only to the scanner on your network and to the Paperless address you give it.
notes: No telemetry, analytics, or upstream accounts.
Scans are held in this app's own storage only until Paperless accepts them.
The scanner's certificate is not verified by default; Epson ships a self-signed one with no published fingerprint.

onboarding.title: Starting a scan
onboarding.summary: Paperless needs to hand you an API token, and scans are started by a request to this app's address.

sections.title: Get the Paperless token
steps: Open Paperless-ngx and sign in as the user the scans should belong to.
Go to the Django admin at /admin/, open Auth Token, and add a token for that user.
Copy the token and paste it into this app's Paperless API token field in Suite Manager.

sections.title: About the scan trigger token
sections.body: MOS generated this token at install. Read it from this app's settings in Suite Manager and put it in the bearer header. Without the header the scan path answers 404, so nothing can start a scan by guessing the address.

sections.title: The scanner's own Scan button does not reach this app
sections.body: Pressing Scan to Computer on the scanner needs the app to receive a broadcast from your home network and to answer a connection from the scanner. MOS gives an app it has not reviewed neither, so the destination never appears on the panel. Start scans with the request above instead, from a phone shortcut, a home-automation rule, or a button.

sections.title: Format and sides
sections.body: Nothing on the panel chooses these when the scan is triggered by a request, so the two setup fields decide. Set sides to duplex only if your scanner has a double-sided feeder; a duplex request to a scanner without one is refused rather than scanned. A single request can override both without changing the settings, as ?format=pdf&sides=simplex on the scan URL.
